utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And could I invite you to restrict yourself, and that applies also to you, Mr. Ostojic, that the purpose of this exercise at this point in time is in relation to the Rule 98 bis process. Eventually -- they are MFI'd at the moment, and any document that is in the record which is MFI'd is still in the record, so eventually what you have stated may become an issue later, later on, but not necessarily for the purpose of Rule 98 bis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. I could just clear up a couple of things that he's brought up. If we could have 65 ter 2103 brought up, page 218. Or Janet can show it, but what that is, as it's coming up -- there it is. It's 219. As you recall the testimony of Mr. Butler, we were provided this material in a format where we could put -- or he could put and OTP could put markings over the top of it, and that's what he did on this particular diagram. And if you recall, he testified about this, saying he had looked at the original US material that was provided to him, but he didn't have it in electronic format, so he wrote in some of this material from the original US. I have the now original US, and based on this challenge, I would like to offer it into evidence so that you can see the actual US markings, which are the same as -- in many respects, the same as the witness. And also on just the last point, could we go to the -- it's the picture of the Pilica dom, page 236. Now, I won't take much time on this, but this is just to illustrate to you the difference between the evidence in this case and what Mr. Ostojic has referred to. Here we have a shot, an aerial image looking down at the Pilica dom. Now, as you know, the Trial Chamber has been there, and you may recollect the dom, and I'm sure you'll recollect the testimony of the witness that was here a day or two ago, Mr. Tomic, who testified that on the 17th of July, the date of this image, he parked his truck at an angle to the door that is on this image, and that his truck became full of bodies and he drove it away. You may also remember the other side door that you saw when -- I believe you saw when we went to the area. And take a look at those traces, as Mr. Ruez calls them, that goes around to the side door, traces or tracks from a truck. You will also remember the 17 July log or log record that shows the -- Mr. Tomic's TAM 130 going and making several trips from, I think it was -- to Pilica and other areas. So you may also remember the old fellows that I -- one of them, I believe he testified he went to the Pilica dom and was partaking in the loading of bodies. And that's just what's off the top of my head tonight on one particular photograph. So we can look at this photograph and we can look into this truck, and we know precisely what was in that truck, what was going on, what date. We have documents, we have witnesses, we've got a plethora of evidence, and I could bring up aerial image after aerial image after aerial image and provide you similar kind of very reliable information. And regarding the altering, Mr. Butler's testified that he -- he blocked out one date on the Bratunac photo because he didn't want the date to be why people looked at this. He said he did that once and that one time and he was cross-examined on it. And that's the only part where he used a white block-out to put over the top of a date, and the rest of it, his additions are all done in a colour, usually yellow, and they're very clear. So that's what I have to say about aerial images.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you wish to respond, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I do take the Court's instruction to restrict myself, although --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down, Mr. Ostojic, please, for the sake of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- to restrict myself and speak slower, obviously. I don't think he addressed the issue, Your Honour, when it comes to the reliability or authenticity of the document. He can wave to us what he purports to be an original document. I think if you look -- and for us, based on your request, we're looking at the July 14th, 1995, aerial image which purports to have an approximate time of 1400 hours. I suggest because my learned friend says he has an enormous amount of documents on all these issues, that this would be simply additional information that is unnecessary for the Court and doesn't assist the Court at all, given what both Mr. Ruez and Mr. Butler have said. If he indeed does have all that evidence, then this is certainly surplus that is unnecessary and cumulative for this trial. We do object to all the aerial images on the same grounds, but particularly those that involve the 14th of July, 1995, in answer to the Court's specific question. We don't believe it purports to indicate what they claim it does. They can argue that they have witnesses that should suffice for their purposes. We don't believe that that is one of the only aerial image that purports to have the time, whereas the other ones don't. With that in mind, I just want to remind the Court that they didn't address the objection as to whether it was authentic, or reliable, or the inconsistency between Mr. Butler's testimony and Mr. Ruez's testimony, so for those same reasons we would ask that the Court not accept this into evidence in regard to the 98 bis or at any time during this trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Does anyone else from the Defence team object to the aerial images or, for that matter, insist on their admission? I'm not trying to put one against the other, but since extensive use has been made with various witnesses of these aerial images, or some of them, both by the Prosecution and by various Defence teams, I think the question is very pertinent. Absolute silence. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't believe we have any aerial images from the 14th of July, so there may be another date that he's concerned about. The 13th of July is when all those people are along the road, if that's what he's concerned with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think we need to stop here today. There are several other matters that we need to discuss tomorrow, but tomorrow I suppose we'll be here for a limited time. Yes, Ms. Nikolic and then Mr. Haynes, and very quickly, please, very briefly. Yes, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Briefly, Your Honour, there is one request pursuant to 92 quater that some of the other teams back as well. In view of the short time limits and the decision of the Trial Chamber with regard to the bearing of two 92 quater applications onto 98 bis motions, we would like an extension by seven days to respond to 92 quater. We consulted with our learned friends from the OTP, and they do not oppose this, and can therefore our response to that filing be filed by the 20th of February, at the latest?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it just you or other Defence teams?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: It's all of us, Your Honour, and indeed we are endeavouring to do this as a combined effort. So though we can't promise this, the likelihood is there will only be one filing from all seven accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. McCloskey. Thank you, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's correct. Given that you've taken this group out of play, the time frame for us was not an issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Permission granted. Time extended to the 20th of February. Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I was simply going to ask that before we arrive here at 2.15 tomorrow, we've got some sort of agenda as to what we've got to talk about. There are a lot of issues floating out there. It can be circulated by e-mail, Your Honours, to save the trouble tonight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We'll do that first thing tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Part of it you already have.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. I've made some notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. There isn't much more, but there's the Rupert Smith matter that needs to be decided and a few other things. So have a nice evening. See you tomorrow afternoon at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
